$comment: Baseline for the migration-lag gate (scripts/check-migration-lag.mjs, `npm run db:lag`).
The gate compares the migration filenames committed in this repo against the names a
database has recorded in its `d1_migrations` table. A name the database has applied that
this repo no longer contains normally means someone applied SQL out of band, and the gate
fails. There is exactly one legitimate reason for such a name: a squashed or rebuilt
migration chain leaves the pre-rebuild filenames in `d1_migrations` forever, because
wrangler never deletes a row from that table. This file is where those names are declared,
per database, so the gate can subtract them on a visible line instead of failing.
SHAPE — one key per database, keyed by the gate's label:
{ "<label>": { "acceptedExtra": ["<pre-rebuild-filename>.sql", ...] } }
The label is `--label` when the npm script passes one (`saas`, `local-d1`), otherwise it is
derived: `<binding> (<wrangler config>, remote|local)` — e.g. `DB (wrangler.local.jsonc,
remote)` for a standalone self-host running `npm run db:lag`. Keys not listed here read as
an empty allowlist, which is the safe default: every unexpected name fails.
WHY EVERY LIST BELOW IS EMPTY. This deployment reconciled the baseline rebuild by rewriting
the ledger rather than by allowlisting: the rows naming the superseded migrations were
deleted, leaving only `0000_baseline.sql`, which wrangler already considers applied. Nothing
is left for the gate to forgive. An empty list is a declaration, not an oversight — and a
declared name that the database no longer carries fails the gate as a stale allowlist, so
these lists must be emptied again whenever a ledger is rewritten.
ADD A NAME HERE ONLY IF you deliberately chose to leave the pre-rebuild rows in place, and
only after confirming that the database's SCHEMA is current. This file silences a report; it
reconciles nothing. Self-hosters upgrading across the baseline rebuild should follow
docs/self-host/upgrade.md instead — the ledger rewrite it describes leaves this file empty.
